EDC Orlando 2026 Lineup Breakdown: A House & Techno Takeover

By PLURGASM @plurgasm ⏱ 4 min read

The festival has happened: read our EDC Orlando 2026 recap and best sets.

The wait is over. EDC Orlando just dropped its 2026 lineup, and the rave internet lit up within minutes. Returning to Tinker Field from November 6–8 for its 15th edition (all under the new kineticJOURNEY theme carried over from EDC Las Vegas' 30th anniversary), this year's bill runs more than 100 artists deep. Here's our honest breakdown of what stands out, and what's quietly missing.

The mainstage is absolutely stacked

Insomniac did not come to play. The top of the bill reads like a festival-house hall of fame: Martin Garrix, David Guetta, Hardwell, Alesso, Kaskade, Afrojack, Steve Aoki, Alan Walker, and Alison Wonderland. David Guetta in particular is a rare get for a US festival outside of Vegas and Ultra, so seeing him on an Orlando bill turned a lot of heads. Add sunset sets from Alesso, Alan Walker, Adventure Club, SLANDER, and Of The Trees, and the marquee alone could carry the weekend.

House and techno are the real winners

If there's a clear theme this year, it's that house and techno absolutely run the lineup. On the house side you've got Chris Lorenzo, Mau P, Disco Lines, Meduza, KREAM, Marlon Hoffstadt, Franky Rizardo, Joshwa, and Dennis Cruz. The techno and hard-techno contingent is even more notable: I Hate Models, Nico Moreno, Holy Priest, Klangkuenstler, Maddix, SHDW, and a Boys Noize b2b Brutalismus 3000 set that reads like a dark-techno fever dream. The back-to-backs are a highlight all on their own: Deorro b2b Diesel, Bou b2b Kanine, Prospa b2b Josh Baker, and ACRAZE b2b CID. House and techno heads are eating very, very well.

Bass heads, we need to talk

Here's where the conversation gets spicy. Compared to recent years, the dubstep and riddim presence is noticeably lighter. There are still heaters: Jessica Audiffred, Kompany, Level Up, Wooli, Ray Volpe, ATLiens, the Skull Machine project (Black Tiger Sex Machine x Kai Wachi), and a "Wholesome Riddim" set from San Holo. But the depth isn't what bass fans have come to expect from Orlando.

And then there's the elephant in the room: Subtronics isn't on the lineup. After becoming a near-annual fixture at EDC Orlando, his absence is easily the most talked-about omission of the drop, and bassheads are not thrilled. One quick PSA to save you some confusion: Subsonic, who is on the bill, is a drum & bass artist, not Subtronics. Easy mix-up, very different set.

No trance this year

Worth flagging for the uplifting crowd: there's essentially no trance presence on this lineup. No Tiësto, no Armin, no dedicated trance day. It's part of a broader trend at EDC's regional events, but trance fans are coming up empty in Orlando this year.

New for 2026: Hotel EDC comes east

The biggest non-music news is Hotel EDC Orlando, the first East Coast version of Insomniac's luxury festival hotel concept, taking over the Margaritaville Resort from November 6–9 in partnership with Vibee. Think festival-themed rooms, onsite concierge, and exclusive daytime and after-party events. If you've ever wanted the full immersive experience without the 4am drive home, this is it.

The details

EDC Orlando 2026 hits Tinker Field on November 6–8, 18+. Three-day GA, GA+, and 21+ VIP tickets go on sale Thursday, June 25 at 12pm EST through Insomniac. Stage takeovers come courtesy of Factory 93 and Bassrush, all under the kineticJOURNEY banner.

Genre gripes aside, this is one of the deepest Orlando bills in years, and as the poster reminds everyone, the most important headliner of all is still you. Add it to your calendar and start planning your sets.
